sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 9.1% a year from FY2016 to FY2025, rising from $23.7 billion to $51.8 billion [F1][F10][F168], but the path was a commodity cycle rather than a smooth trend.

The window contains two deep troughs and one spike: revenue fell 58.0% in FY2020 to $13.7 billion [F5][D161], then rose 153.2% in FY2021 to $34.6 billion [F6][D200] and 76.5% in FY2022 to $61.0 billion [F7][D238], before falling 20.5% in FY2023 to $48.5 billion [F8][D274].
The FY2023 decline came from lower realized commodity prices across all products, partly offset by higher sales volumes [P40][P47][F8].
The FY2022 surge reflected higher realized commodity prices and higher sales volumes, primarily from the Shell Permian acquisition [P59][F7].

The table's revenue is a later recast, not the figure first reported — FY2025 shows $51.8 billion here against $58.9 billion in that year's 10-K [F10][X10] — so growth rates that mix recast and never-recast years compare two presentations [R1].
Crude oil is the dominant line, at 66.3% of revenue in FY2025 [D551], and it contributed just 0.1pp of the 4.9% revenue growth that year [D553][D342].

The U.S. geography supplied 79.1% of revenue and +5.7pp of FY2025 growth [D382][D384], while natural gas added +4.4pp on 37.4% growth [D586][D585] and the Pipeline Company subtracted 2.6pp on a 20.9% decline [D621][D620].

Sales and other operating revenues rose $4.2 billion in FY2025 on higher volumes of $6.2 billion, including Marathon Oil volumes, and higher realized gas prices of $824 million, partly offset by lower realized crude and bitumen prices of $4.6 billion and $349 million [P28][F10].

Profit did not keep pace: net income fell 13.6% to $8.0 billion [F20][D343] while revenue rose 4.9% [D342], and diluted EPS fell 18.7% to $6.35 [F49][D345] against a 6.1% larger diluted share count [D356].
The earnings squeeze came from higher DD&A of $1.3 billion and higher production and operating expenses of $875 million, both driven by the Marathon Oil acquisition [P17][F20].
Net margin was 15.4% in FY2025 [F30], below the 17.9% window median [D831] and far under the 30.6% FY2022 high [D830], though still above the 8.1% energy peer median [D847].

The latest year's 3.3pp net-margin decline [D351] came with D&A at 19.5% of revenue [D330] and cost of revenue at 37.9% [D326], the latter up from 36.6% as cost of revenue grew 11.6% against 4.9% revenue growth [D292][D352][D342].

DD&A rose $1.9 billion in FY2025 on the Marathon Oil acquisition and higher production volumes [P22][X61], and production and operating expenses rose $1.6 billion on the same acquisition plus $216 million of restructuring severance [P24].
SG&A fell $265 million, mainly the absence of $545 million of Marathon transaction expenses in FY2024, partly offset by severance [P23][X50].
Below the line, the effective tax rate rose to 36.9% [D332] and net interest expense increased on debt assumed from Marathon [P10][X81], widening the gap between operating and net results.
Operating cash flow was $19.8 billion in FY2025 [F59], 2.48x net income [D333] and 33.6% of revenue [D331], well above the 18.1% of FY2016 [D8].
The 1.6% decline in operating cash flow [D346] came from lower commodity prices, mostly offset by operations from the 2024 Marathon Oil acquisition [P6][F59].
Free cash flow is only reported through FY2022, when it was $18.2 billion, a 23.1% margin [F73][D223], against a 12.2% window median [D834]; capex that year was 1.35x D&A [D228].
Stock-based compensation is small, 1.7% of operating cash flow in FY2025 [D334], so conversion is driven by commodity prices and working capital rather than equity pay.
The company held net cash of $7.1 billion at FY2025, 12.1% of revenue [D337][D338], the 100th percentile against six energy peers whose median is net debt of 7.7% of revenue [D850][D851].
Cash and investments were $8.1 billion against $1.0 billion of total debt [D335][D336], and the current ratio was 1.30x [F153], below its 1.45x window median [D843].

In FY2025 the company used $12.6 billion for capital expenditures and investments, $5.0 billion for buybacks, $4.0 billion for the dividend and $0.9 billion to retire debt, partly offset by $3.2 billion of asset sale proceeds [P7][X141][X151][X178].
Buybacks plus dividends of $9.0 billion were 46% of operating cash flow [D339][P31], and the diluted share count still rose 6.1% in FY2025 [D356], so repurchases did not offset issuance.
Return on average equity fell to 12.4% [D341], below the 14.9% peer median [D853], as the equity base built up after the Marathon deal.

The recast revenue basis is the flag that matters most: every year in the table differs from its first-reported figure [R1][F1][X1][F10][X10], so any growth or margin comparison spanning a recast and a never-recast year mixes presentations and should not anchor a conclusion.

The FY2023 revenue decline of 20.5% [R2][D274] was a price-driven cyclical fall, explained by lower realized commodity prices partly offset by higher volumes [P40][P47], and revenue has since recovered 4.9% in FY2025 [D342].
The FY2017 SG&A restatement is minor [R3][X42], and the segment-member overlap [R4] means segment shares should be read individually, not summed.
Watch net margin against the 17.9% window median [D831]: a print above it in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the margin slide from the 30.6% FY2022 high [D830] has stopped.
Watch operating cash flow against the $19.8 billion FY2025 level [F59]: a further decline would confirm the commodity-price pressure cited for FY2025 [P6], while a recovery above it would reverse it.
Watch the diluted share count against 1,253.4 million shares [X131]: continued growth above that level would show buybacks of $5.0 billion [X141] failing to offset issuance.
Watch net cash against the $7.1 billion FY2025 level [D337]: a move toward the peer median of net debt at 7.7% of revenue [D851] would signal the balance-sheet advantage is eroding.
